audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is missing entirely: Ground Slam 'reduces the Attack Speed of enemies', on a flat 7-second cooldown. Not one string on the page mentions it. Olaf's passive is attack speed and lifesteal, his W adds attack speed, and his damage is autos — Malphite's E is a direct tax on Olaf's entire engine, available every 7 seconds. Also missing: Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health and recharges when he has not been hit, so an unpoked Malphite gets the first tenth of his health bar free. Three strings say Ragnarok 'cleanses' Unstoppable Force; Riot's text is immunity to disables while attacking, which means it has to be active BEFORE the knock-up lands, not pressed after. Seismic Shard is called 'a single long-cooldown slow' twice — it is a flat 8s at every rank, and it steals the move speed it takes.
audit.why: A player reading this page thinks their only job is to dodge one ultimate. In reality they lose a chunk of their attack speed every 7 seconds — which is also their lifesteal, since Berserker Rage's healing rides on attacks landing — and they open every trade into a shield that regenerates for free if they respect the lane too much. The cleanse framing is the same timing reversal the mirror agent found: press Ragnarok after the knock-up and you have already been knocked up.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam's 7s attack-speed cut written into report[5].t, whys[2], wants.foe[1], content.early and content.mid. Granite Shield's 10% written into spikes[0].text and wants.you[1]. Ragnarok rewritten as must-already-be-up in dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why and whys[4]. Seismic Shard's flat 8s replaces 'long cooldown' in content.early. Unstoppable Force's 130s stated.

audit.why: 130s at rank 1 is a long window in which Malphite has no way to flip a losing trade. Naming it turns 'respect his ult' into 'you have two minutes'.
audit.corrected: 130s added in three places; Ground Slam's 7s added as the cooldown that actually governs the trade rhythm.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads into a knock-up ult and Black Cleaver against stacked armour both read correctly, and the page rightly notes Reckless Swing's true damage bypasses his armour entirely.

edits.before: Malphite has no kill pressure on you levels 1-3 and his Q is a single slow-poke on a long early cooldown, so step up and trade freely. Land your Q to stick him, walk in for the E true-damage nuke, and let your passive attack speed ramp as his W-buffed autos chip you. His armor does nothing against E's true damage, and your W omnivamp heals back any Q poke he lands. This is your lane to dictate.
edits.after: Malphite has no kill pressure on you levels 1-3, but don't treat Seismic Shard as rare — it is a flat 8s at every rank and it steals your move speed as it slows. Land your Q to stick him, walk in for the E true-damage nuke, and chip Granite Shield off first so its 10% max-HP layer isn't eating your opener. Watch Ground Slam: 7s, and it cuts the attack speed your damage and lifesteal both run on.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you keep out-trading him, chaining axe-reset slows so he can never walk away, but at 6 you have to respect Ragnarok-on-the-other-side: his R is an unstoppable knock-up that flips a trade he is otherwise losing, so bait it or commit when it is down. With your R up you ignore that knock-up entirely and run him down. Once Black Cleaver comes online his stacked armor is shredded and your E still ignores it outright.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you keep out-trading him with axe-reset slows, but Ground Slam every 7s keeps shaving the attack speed your damage rides on, so favour short bursts over long grinds. At 6 his 130s knock-up flips a trade he is otherwise losing — the answer is to already be in Ragnarok when he presses it, not to press yours afterwards. Once Black Cleaver lands his stacked armour is shredded and your E ignores it outright.

notes: Ground Slam was the find here: an attack-speed reduction on a flat 7-second cooldown, aimed squarely at a champion whose passive, W and lifesteal are all attack speed, and it appeared in exactly zero of the page's forty-plus strings. Granite Shield's 10% max-HP absorb was likewise never mentioned, which matters because it recharges out of combat — the player who 'respects the lane' hands it back for free every wave. Both are now on the page. The 'R cleanses it' framing is the same timing reversal the mirror agent flagged, and it appeared here in three strings. dosFull[2].t still reads 'R to cleanse his combo' (22 characters, under the applier's skip threshold) so that one needs a manual edit.
